topic: The Mirror World of Graphs: Duality and Euler’s Formula
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Planar Landscape
lecture_lines: A planar graph's edges never cross on a plane.
It has vertices, edges, and bounded or unbounded faces.
This house graph has vertices, edges, and faces.
It has five vertices, six edges, and three faces.
Euler's formula: V minus E plus F equals two.
animations: Draw a 'House' graph with 5 light blue (#ADD8E6) vertices and 6 edges.
Fill the 3 regions (faces) with a soft green (#90EE90) glow.
Label each vertex (V), edge (E), and face (F) with white (#FFFFFF) text.
Scale up the text 'V - E + F = 2' while substituting counts 5, 6, 3.
Flash the 'infinite' outer face to emphasize it counts as a face.

sections.title: The Birth of the Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Every planar graph has a unique dual companion.
Duality transforms the original structure into a new graph.
Place a dual vertex inside every original face.
animations: Dim the original 'House' graph [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/house.svg] to light gray (#D3D3D3).
Place 3 bright red (#FF0000) dots in the center of each face.
Label these red dots as Dual Vertices (V*) in white (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: The Bridge: Connecting the Dual
lecture_lines: Connect dual vertices where original faces share an edge.
One dual edge crosses exactly one original edge.
The number of edges remains exactly the same.
animations: Draw orange (#FFA500) dual edges crossing each original edge to connect dual vertices.

Highlight one original 'fence' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fence.svg] edge and its crossing orange 'bridge' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg] edge.
Count all 6 orange dual edges and show E* = 6.

sections.title: Mathematical Symmetry & Euler's Swap
lecture_lines: Dual vertices correspond to the original graph's faces.
Dual faces correspond to the original graph's vertices.
Symmetry preserves Euler's formula in the dual graph.
animations: Display the Original graph (left) and Dual graph (right) on a split screen.
Color-code and link V=5 to F*=5 and F=3 to V*=3 using arrows.
Flash the orange edges (E=6 and E*=6) to show they are identical.
Animate the dual Euler formula: 3 - 6 + 5 = 2 at the bottom.
Highlight the symmetry by swapping the left and right graph positions.

sections.title: Application: Mazes and Circuitry
lecture_lines: Duality simplifies complex layouts in circuit board design.
Mazes use duality to define walls and paths.
If walls form a tree, the path always exits.
animations: Show a grid maze [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/maze.svg] with walls in blue (#0000FF).
Transform the paths into a dual graph [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/circuit.svg] in yellow (#FFFF00).
Animate a yellow circle moving along the dual path to the exit.
